question: What percentage of the vote will the Massachusetts initiative to repeal recreational marijuana legalization receive?

calls.reasoning: Four polls (Sep–Oct 2026) put Yes at 21–31% raw, about 23–34% after dropping undecideds, averaging ~28%. In past cannabis ballot measures the polls tended to overstate the pro-cannabis side (FL 2024), and the repeal side outspends the No side ($3.5M from SAM vs $2.3M), which argues for a few points above the poll average. Pushing the other way: undecideds on long ballots tend to vote No, and Democrats oppose the measure 80%. 2016 legalization passed 53.7%, so ~46% opposed then. No prediction market found (Kalshi, Polymarket and Manifold checked; both Kalshi and Polymarket are in legal fights with MA). Median 31%.
calls.dossier:
- What Question 8 does: a Yes vote ends adult-use retail sales. Medical marijuana and possession of up to 1 oz stay legal; home grow stays legal per WBUR (another summary says otherwise). Takes effect 2028. Ballot wording for Yes: 'prohibit the legalization, regulation, and taxation of the retail sale of adult recreational use marijuana' (WBUR, 2026-10-09).
- Suffolk/Boston Globe, 500 likely voters, Oct 14-18 2026: Yes 21.4, No 71.4, undecided 5.8. By party: Democrats 80% No; independents 73% No; Republicans 46 Yes / 44 No (Forbes, NORML, Marijuana Herald, Oct 2026).
- UMass Amherst/WCVB, 800+ registered voters, Oct 5-14 2026: Yes 31, No 61 (Forbes 2026-10-20).
- CommonWealth Beacon/MassINC, likely voters, Sept 2026: Yes 27, No 61.
- UNH Bay State Poll, likely voters, Sept 2026: Yes 24, No 71.
- Two-way Yes shares from these polls: about 23, 34, 31, 25.
- Money (WBUR, Oct 9): Yes committee ~$3.5M, almost all from Smart Approaches to Marijuana Action; No committee ~$2.3M (industry groups, Retailers Association of MA). Dozens of legislators and the Worcester mayor urge a No vote.
- Baseline: MA 2016 Question 4 (legalization) passed 53.7-46.3.
- Past cannabis measures: final polls often overstated the pro-cannabis side (FL 2024 polled ~60-65%, got ~56%).
- Nine questions are on the 2026 MA ballot; this one has the lowest support in polls.
- Status quo: No wins. Resolves off the certified percentage of valid Yes votes on Q8 (per Ballotpedia), not off polls. Event: the Nov 3 2026 election; vote count not yet started as of Oct 24.
- Searched for but not found: any prediction market (Kalshi, Polymarket, Manifold); later polls after Oct 18.
calls.reference_class: Recent state cannabis ballot measures, comparing final polls with results, plus the MA 2016 Question 4 baseline

calls.reasoning: Reference class: lopsided-losing state ballot measures in the final 2 weeks, where the result usually lands near or a little above the poll's two-party yes share. Polls: UNH Sept 24-71, a Sept poll at 27% yes, UMass/WCVB Oct 5-12 31-61, Suffolk/Globe Oct 20 21.4-71.4. Excluding undecideds, yes is 23-34%, median about 28%. Some upward drift is plausible: undecideds and confusion over what a 'yes to repeal' vote means, plus the 46% who voted no on legalization in 2016, which marks a ceiling for latent opposition. Against that, Democrats are strongly opposed, legislators are pushing No, and the No campaign likely has a funding edge. Median 30%. Little chance of exceeding 50.5%. Small tail below 19.5% if the Suffolk number is right and No gains further. No prediction market found on Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold.
calls.dossier:
- Q8 (MA 2026) would repeal adult-use retail cannabis sales and home cultivation, keeping limited possession. Election is Nov 3, 2026. Resolves off the official % of valid votes cast YES, rounded to the nearest point (Ballotpedia page).
- UNH poll (reported Sept 25, 2026, NORML): 24% yes, 71% no. A spring 2026 UNH poll had 63% no.
- Marijuana Herald mentions a Sept 2026 MA poll with 27% of likely voters supporting repeal.
- UMass Amherst/WCVB poll, Oct 5-12, 2026, 800 registered voters: 31% yes, 61% no; 47% of all voters said they were definitely voting no (Ganjapreneur).
- Suffolk/Boston Globe poll, released Oct 20, 2026, 500 likely voters, MOE ±4.4: 21.4% yes, 71.4% no, 5.8% undecided. Republicans 46 yes / 44 no; Democrats 80% no; independents 73% no.
- UMass poll (Oct 21) found voters see legalization as positive for the economy, tax revenue and criminal justice.
- Dozens of MA legislators urged a No vote (NORML, Oct 22). The Yes campaign's money reportedly comes almost entirely from one out-of-state anti-cannabis group; dollar amounts not found.
- History: 2016 Q4 legalization passed 53.7-46.3. No state has yet repealed legal adult-use cannabis by ballot.
- Status quo: legal market remains; the question is only the Yes margin.
- Event window: votes cast through Nov 3, 2026; counting/certification after. As of Oct 24, the campaign is about 90% elapsed.
- Searched without finding: Kalshi/Polymarket/Manifold markets on Q8, and spending totals.
calls.reference_class: Massachusetts/state ballot measures polling ~25% yes two weeks out; result vs. two-party poll share

calls.reasoning: Three Oct 2026 polls: UMass/WCVB 31-61, Suffolk/Globe 21-71, UNH 24-71; average Yes ~25%, two-way ~27%. Lopsided ballot measures typically finish less lopsided than polls, and 46% opposed legalization in 2016, so the Yes floor is not tiny. Repeals of voter-approved laws generally do worse than the original opposition; positive views of legalization and out-of-state dark-money funding cap Yes. No human market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmakers. Median ~31%.
calls.dossier:
- Measure: Question 8 (2026) would end retail adult-use cannabis sales in Massachusetts but keep adult possession and medical sales legal. A Yes vote is for repeal. (NORML/WGBH, Oct 2026)
- Poll: UMass Amherst/WCVB, Oct 5-12 2026, 800 registered voters: 31% Yes, 61% No. Yes support 44% among Republicans, 46% among conservatives, 41% among non-users. (Ganjapreneur)
- Poll: Suffolk/Boston Globe, released Oct 20 2026, 500 likely voters: 21.4% Yes, 71.4% No. (Marijuana Herald)
- Poll: UNH, fall 2026: 24% Yes, 71% No. (search-result summary)
- UMass poll (Oct 21): most voters say legalization has been positive for the economy, tax revenue, communities and criminal justice. (Marijuana Moment/NORML)
- Money: the Yes committee (Coalition for a Healthy Massachusetts) raised about $3.53M, 98.5% from SAM Action (Virginia, undisclosed donors), and has spent over $3.6M including TV and digital ads. (Fall River Reporter; WGBH, Oct 8 2026)
- Opposition: dozens of state lawmakers urged a No vote (NORML, Oct 22 2026). No-side spending figures were searched for but not found.
- History: 2016 Question 4 (legalization) passed 53.7% to 46.3%. No US state has ever repealed voter-approved adult-use legalization by ballot.
- Pattern: lopsided ballot-measure polls often narrow by Election Day, and undecided voters often break No on initiatives. These two effects pull in opposite directions here.
- Status quo: legal sales continue (No wins).
- Resolves off the official certified Yes percentage of valid votes on MA Question 8, rounded to the nearest point (per Ballotpedia).
- Event window: Election Day Nov 3 2026 to certified results, resolution about Nov 10. As of Oct 24 the vote has not happened (early voting in progress).
- Searched for but not found: Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold markets; No-campaign fundraising totals; an aggregate polling average.
calls.reference_class: Massachusetts ballot questions with lopsided October polling (final Yes vs poll Yes share), anchored on 2016 Q4 opposition (46.3%) as a ceiling for a repeal

calls.reasoning: Polls Sep-Oct 2026: Suffolk/Globe 21-71, UMass/WCVB 31-61 (RV), MassINC 27-61, UNH 24-71; two-way Yes ~23-34, likely-voter mean ~26. Lopsided measures tend to finish closer than polls, and anti-cannabis sides have historically outperformed polls (FL 2024), with Yes funded at least comparably. Countervailing: strong Democratic opposition, legislators pushing No, out-of-state dark-money framing, 2016 opposition of 46% as soft ceiling. Median ~30.5. No human prediction market found by any run (Kalshi/Polymarket/Manifold/bookmakers).
calls.reconciliation: Runs agreed closely (medians 30-31, widths 12-13.5). Factual disputes: home-grow provision (immaterial to vote share, unsettleable without web); No-side funding ($2.3M per Run 1 vs not found by others) — immaterial, all agree Yes funding is at least comparable. Judgment: size of upward drift from poll average (~26-28) toward result; I accept a ~3-pt drift based on cannabis-measure poll-error history, landing at 30.5, slightly widening tails given poll spread (21-31 raw). No web access this run.
